come_follow_me.title: “There Is No Other God That Can Deliver”
come_follow_me.summary: Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego were young men taken captive to Babylon. They kept their covenants by praying, fasting, choosing good friends, trusting God, and being a light to others—even when a king threatened a fiery furnace or a den of lions. God delivered them, showed Daniel a dream of a stone cut without hands that became a mountain and filled the earth (the Lord’s latter-day Church), and revealed the Son of Man receiving an everlasting kingdom.
questions: How can I trust the Lord when my faith is tried? (Daniel 1; 3; 6)
What does Nebuchadnezzar’s dream teach about the Lord’s Church? (Daniel 2:34–35, 44–45)
Why was praying so important to Daniel, and why does it matter to me? (Daniel 6:10)

daily.quote: Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself
daily.thought: Daniel decided ahead of time to keep God’s standards, even in the king’s palace. What’s one standard we can decide now to keep this week?

daily.quote: our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace
daily.thought: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego knew God could save them. When has Heavenly Father helped you through something scary?

daily.quote: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods
daily.thought: They would choose God even if He didn’t deliver them the way they hoped. How can we choose the right when we don’t know how things will turn out?

daily.quote: the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed
daily.thought: The stone in the king’s dream is the Lord’s Church. What’s one way our family can help it grow?

daily.quote: he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God
daily.thought: A new law made prayer illegal, but Daniel prayed just as he always had. Where is one place we can remember to pray today?

daily.quote: the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth
daily.thought: God’s kingdom started small and will fill the earth. What small kind thing could we do today?

daily.quote: there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom
daily.thought: Daniel saw Jesus Christ, the Son of Man, receive an everlasting kingdom. How does that change how we feel about following Him?

deep_dive.intro: Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego were taken captive as young men by Babylon. Surrounded by a different culture, they faced great temptations to abandon their beliefs, yet they remained true by doing small and simple things—praying, fasting, choosing good friends, trusting God, and being a light to others. God worked miracles that still inspire believers today.

scripture_blocks.about: Daniel and his friends refuse the king’s food and God gives them knowledge
Nebuchadnezzar’s dream of the statue and the stone that fills the earth
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego in the fiery furnace
Daniel prays and is delivered from the lions’ den
Daniel’s vision of the Son of Man receiving an everlasting kingdom

principles.title: I can trust in the Lord when my faith is tried.
principles.explain: Daniel and his friends were pressured to eat the king’s food, bow to a gold statue, and stop praying. They chose God anyway—even if He did not deliver them the way they hoped (“But if not”). Jesus will help us do what is right when it is hard.

principles.title: Heavenly Father wants me to take care of my body.
principles.explain: Daniel asked to eat simple food (pulse and water) instead of the king’s meat and wine. After ten days they looked healthier, and God gave them knowledge and wisdom. Heavenly Father’s law of health today, the Word of Wisdom, blesses our bodies and minds too.

principles.title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is the kingdom of God on earth.
principles.explain: King Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a huge statue smashed by a stone cut out without hands. The stone grew into a mountain that filled the whole earth. That stone is the Lord’s Church, set up by God, and it will never be destroyed. We each have a part in helping it roll forth.

principles.title: Receiving revelation requires spiritual preparation.
principles.explain: When the king ordered the wise men killed, Daniel asked his friends to pray for mercies from God. God revealed the dream in a night vision, and Daniel gave the credit to Heavenly Father, not himself. Revelation comes when we prepare—praying, living worthy, and being humble.

principles.title: Heavenly Father wants me to pray often.
principles.explain: A new law said anyone who prayed to God would be thrown to the lions. Daniel still knelt and prayed three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem, just as he always had. We can pray anywhere, anytime—and Heavenly Father hears us.

key_verses.text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.

If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.

I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.

quote.text: Like Joseph in Egypt and Esther in Persia, Daniel and his friends in Babylon kept their faith in God, and God worked miracles that still inspire believers to this day.
quote.by: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026, Nov. 9–15

questions: When have you felt pressured to do something you knew was wrong? How has the Lord blessed you for keeping His commandments? (Daniel 1; 3; 6)
What if your faith doesn’t lead to the miracles you seek? How can Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego’s example affect how you approach your trials? (Daniel 3:13–18)
How can your righteous choices lead others to greater faith in the Lord? (Daniel 2:47; 3:28–29)
What is your role in helping this prophecy come to pass—the stone that fills the earth? (Daniel 2:34–35, 44–45)
Why was praying to Heavenly Father so important to Daniel? Why is praying important to you? (Daniel 6)

activity.title: Story pictures: choose the right
activity.steps: Find or draw pictures of Daniel and his friends refusing the king’s food (Daniel 1), Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego in the fiery furnace (Daniel 3), and Daniel in the lions’ den (Daniel 6). Place them face down and take turns flipping one over and telling the story (see this week’s activity page or Gospel Art Book nos. 23, 25, and 26). Then talk about a time you might feel pressured to make a wrong choice, share how the Lord has blessed you for choosing the right, and sing “Choose the Right” (Hymns, no. 239). Bonus: read Daniel 2:31–35, 44–45 and draw Nebuchadnezzar’s dream of the statue and the stone that became a mountain—the stone represents The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

scripture.text: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

deep_dive.intro: Your Heavenly Father is a God of truth. All truth comes from Him and leads to Him. You show that you value truth when you keep learning, live with integrity, and bravely stand for what you know is right.

teachings.title: Always be learning
teachings.explain: Heavenly Father wants His children to keep learning—at school, in training, and from sources you trust. Education isn’t just about money; it’s part of becoming more like Him. Ask the Lord to guide you.

teachings.title: Learn spiritual truths
teachings.explain: While you learn about the world, learn about the Savior who created it. Seminary and personal gospel study help you know Him and prepare to serve a mission and share the gospel.

teachings.title: Live with integrity
teachings.explain: Integrity means loving what is right more than being comfortable or popular. Don’t steal, lie, cheat, or deceive—at school, at work, or online. Be the same person when no one is watching.

teachings.title: You have something precious to share
teachings.explain: The gospel holds answers to life’s questions. You don’t have to know everything—you know enough to love your neighbor, share true principles, and invite friends to learn more.

teachings.title: Questions can build faith
teachings.explain: Having questions isn’t weakness. Joseph Smith was 14 when he asked a question with faith. Look for answers in the scriptures, the prophets, family, leaders, and God—and keep living what you already know.

quotes: Living with integrity means you love what is right in the sight of God—more than you love personal comfort, popularity, or convenience. It means doing what is right simply because it is right.
Be the same faithful follower of Jesus Christ in public and in private.
When you stand up for the teachings of Jesus Christ, He stands with you. Jesus Christ is your strength!
deep_dive.blessings: Education increases your ability to serve the Lord, including as a missionary. It empowers you to bless others, especially your family. The more you learn, the more you can help build God’s kingdom and influence the world for good.
questions: Why does God want you to learn about Him and the world around you?
What should you do when you have questions?
Do you strive to be honest in all that you do?
Am I the same follower of Jesus Christ online and in private as I am at church?
How can I stand up for what is right without being unkind to people who believe differently?
